reviewType: independent automated visual inspection, not trainer certification

observations: Full body and support visible; hand grip and stable left/image-left shoe anatomically plausible; character and logo match.
Raised foot is slightly above floor, suitable elevation.
Yellow arrow is a HORIZONTAL ellipse around the lower shin/ankle. It reads as rotation of the whole leg about a vertical axis, rather than toe-led ankle circumduction.
requiredFixes: Replace arrow with a small arc/circle whose path is around the raised toes in a plane near the front of shoe, with knee/shin stationary. A clear ankle-only inset is unnecessary if the arrow can be made unambiguous.

observations: Clear figure-four: one ankle rests across opposite distal thigh above knee; both feet off floor.
Hands reach around/behind the underlying thigh; one arm threads through gap. No force directly on crossed knee.
Head and shoulders supported; two legs and two arms, clothing/logo consistent; one held static pose plus instructions for change of side is sufficient.
Hand gripping elevated shoe, knee deep flexion, single hand and opposite knee support are plausible anatomically.

Torso and pelvis rotate OPEN TOWARD CAMERA substantially, raised thigh also abducts laterally. Reads as a kneeling bow/side-open stretch, rather than quadruped with hips facing floor as intended in prompt.
Supporting hand is laterally offset and trunk leans to side to accommodate pose; this obscures hip-extension focus.
requiredFixes: Regenerate with shoulders and pelvis facing floor/square, support hand under shoulder and knee under hip, lifted thigh extends backward in sagittal plane, heel toward buttock. Keep neutral lumbar spine and minimize trunk rotation.

observations: All3 show same thick bar, two bumper plates per side, silver collars and consistent mixed grip. Despite phase1 prompt saying one plate, actual equipment is consistent.
Ground setup, natural upright endpoint, and controlled hinge lowering are distinct and complete; downward arrow is unambiguous; arms straight, bar close, back appears neutral.
No major hand/anatomical defect found; original identity/clothing/logo retained.
Foot ground baseline shifts from about y840 to y930 to y870 and slight framing changes; not perfectly fixed camera. This is visible but does not reverse or obscure the exercise.
recommendedFixes: If enforcing literal fixed camera, align shoe/floor baselines across all3 with same framing; otherwise disclose minor framing variation in checks.
